grammar.title: Type 3 Conditionals — Si + Pluperfect Subjunctive + Conditional Perfect
grammar.content:
Type 3 conditionals express hypothetical situations in the PAST that did NOT happen — regrets, missed opportunities, and alternate histories. This is the most emotionally loaded conditional form in Spanish.

Structure: Si + [pluperfect subjunctive = hubiera/hubiese + past participle], [conditional perfect = habría/habrías/... + past participle]

The pluperfect subjunctive is formed from the imperfect subjunctive of HABER + the past participle of the main verb.
The conditional perfect uses the conditional of HABER + the past participle.

Uses:
- Expressing regret: Si hubiera estudiado más, habría aprobado el examen
- Describing missed opportunities: Si hubiéramos salido antes, no nos habríamos perdido el tren
- Speculating about the past: ¿Qué habría pasado si no nos hubiéramos conocido?

⚠️ CRITICAL ERROR TO AVOID: Never put the conditional perfect after 'si'. 'Si habría sabido' is grammatically incorrect. The correct form is 'Si hubiera sabido'.

rows: Si hubiera llovido, habría quedado en casa
Habría venido si hubiera sabido que estabas

examples: Si hubiera sabido que venías, habría preparado algo. (If I had known you were coming, I would have prepared something.)
Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos ido a la playa. (If it hadn't rained, we would have gone to the beach.)
¿Qué habría pasado si hubieras aceptado el trabajo? (What would have happened if you had accepted the job?)
Me habría encantado haber visto la obra de teatro. (I would have loved to have seen the play.)
Si hubiéramos salido antes, no nos habríamos perdido el vuelo. (If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the flight.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian Type 3: 'Dacă aș fi știut, aș fi venit' — the mapping is: 'dacă' = 'si', 'aș fi știut' = pluperfect subjunctive equivalent, 'aș fi venit' = conditional perfect. The Romanian 'să fi + participiu' and Spanish 'hubiera + participio' serve the same hypothetical past function.

pronunciation.title: Stress in Compound Conditionals
pronunciation.content:
Compound conditional forms have two stressed syllables:

- hubiera sabido (oo-BYE-ra sa-BÍ-do) — stress on 'bie' and 'bi'
- habría venido (ah-BRÍ-a be-NÍ-do) — stress on 'rí' and 'ni'
- hubiéramos salido (oo-BYE-ra-mos sa-LÍ-do) — stress on 'ye' and 'li'

The 'hubiera' forms are always stressed on the 'ie': hu-BIE-ra
The 'habría' forms are always stressed on the 'rí': ha-BRÍ-a

When both forms appear in the same sentence:
'Si hubiera sabido, habría venido.' = si oo-BYE-ra sa-BÍ-do, ah-BRÍ-a be-NÍ-do

Critical: Spanish 'hubiera' is pronounced 'oo-BYE-ra' (3 syllables), NOT 'oo-BEE-rah' as English speakers might assume. The 'ie' is a diphthong but the 'ra' at the end is a separate syllable.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian 'aș fi știut' (aSH fi SHTIOOT) and 'aș fi venit' (aSH fi be-NIT) use two words where Spanish uses 'hubiera + participio'. The Romanian version is shorter in syllables but carries the same stress pattern.

exercises.question: Which sentence correctly uses Type 3 conditional structure?
exercises.explanation: Type 3 conditionals: Si + hubiera + participio, habría + participio. 'Si hubiera sabido, habría venido.' Never use the conditional after 'si'.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si ____ (you) ____ (know), ____ (you) ____ (have come).' (If you had known, you would have come.)
exercises.explanation: 'Hubieras sabido' — pluperfect subjunctive. 'Habrías venido' — conditional perfect.

exercises.question: What is the pluperfect subjunctive of 'haber' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hubiera habido' is the pluperfect subjunctive of haber (yo form). Both 'hubiera habido' and 'hubiese habido' are correct — the -ra and -se forms are interchangeable.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Si ____ (we) ____ (have) más tiempo, ____ (we) ____ (would have traveled) más.' (If we had had more time, we would have traveled more.)
exercises.explanation: 'Hubiéramos tenido' — pluperfect subjunctive of tener. 'Habríamos viajado' — conditional perfect of viajar.

exercises.question: What does 'me habría encantado' mean?
exercises.explanation: 'Me habría encantado' = 'I would have loved' — conditional perfect of encantar. Used to express a missed opportunity: 'Me habría encantado verte.'

exercises.question: Complete the reversed Type 3 conditional: '____ (we) ____ (would have missed) el tren si ____ (we) ____ (had left) antes.'
exercises.correct: no nos habríamos perdido hubiéramos salido
exercises.explanation: 'No nos habríamos perdido el tren si hubiéramos salido antes.' Reversed order (no comma needed). Conditional perfect + si + pluperfect subjunctive.
